name: John Sweeney

positions.statement: OPB reported in 2026 that Sweeney wants to let the county oversee the region's homelessness response.
positions.excerpt: let the county oversee the region's homelessness response.

positions.statement: The Portland Mercury reported in 2026 that, during his time on the Multnomah Education Service District board, Sweeney called bilingual education a 'waste of money.'
positions.excerpt: during which time he railed against bilingual education as a 'waste of money.'

positions.statement: In a September 2024 OPB candidate questionnaire for his earlier District 3 run, Sweeney listed increasing and refreshing the Portland Police and Police Reserve as a public safety priority.
positions.excerpt: Public Safety: Increase and refresh the Portland Police and Portland Police Reserve.

positions.statement: In a September 2024 OPB candidate questionnaire for his earlier District 3 run, Sweeney said he would examine the housing system to find roadblocks and then streamline the process.
positions.excerpt: First, I would want to examine the system to locate the roadblocks, then streamline the process

positions.statement: In a September 2024 OPB candidate questionnaire for his earlier District 3 run, Sweeney said there are enough bike and bus lanes and that it is time to fix streets.
positions.excerpt: We have enough bike and bus lanes. It is way past time to fix our streets.

positions.statement: In a September 2024 OPB candidate questionnaire for his earlier District 3 run, Sweeney said the new mayor lacks veto power, which he said means there are no checks and balances.
positions.excerpt: The new Mayor does not have veto power. That means that there is no “checks and balances.”

positions.statement: In a September 2024 OPB candidate questionnaire for his earlier District 3 run, Sweeney said he would end diversity, equity and inclusion efforts.
positions.excerpt: move social services to the county and end diversity, equity and inclusion efforts

positions.statement: In an April 2022 OPB questionnaire for governor candidates, Sweeney proposed reducing fuel such as tall grass and brush along roads to address wildfire.
positions.excerpt: Reduce the fuel (tall grass & brush) a long the roads.

positions.statement: In an April 2022 OPB questionnaire for governor candidates, Sweeney said going to white or light colored roofs would reduce energy use.
positions.excerpt: Going to white or light colored roofs will reduce energy use.

positions.statement: In an April 2022 OPB questionnaire for governor candidates, asked about drought, Sweeney answered that it could be addressed by removing as many juniper trees as possible.
positions.excerpt: By removing as many juniper trees as possible.

positions.statement: In an April 2022 OPB questionnaire for governor candidates, Sweeney said child care is a local matter in which the state should play a supporting role.
positions.excerpt: Again, this is local and the state should be in the supporting role.

positions.statement: In an April 2022 OPB questionnaire for governor candidates, Sweeney said abortion is to be between the woman, doctor and God, and answered no on pushing for new restrictions if Roe v. Wade were overturned.
positions.excerpt: I think this is to be between the woman/doctor/God.

positions.statement: In an April 2022 OPB questionnaire for governor candidates, Sweeney said toll roads and bridges are a bad idea.
positions.excerpt: I think that toll roads 7 bridges are a bad idea.

positions.statement: In an April 2022 OPB questionnaire for governor candidates, Sweeney said body cameras have shown results in crime solving and have helped in public contacts.
positions.excerpt: It has shown results in crime solving and has proved helpful in public contacts.

positions.statement: In an April 2022 OPB questionnaire for governor candidates, Sweeney said cities and counties must do the bulk of the work on homelessness.
positions.excerpt: The cities & counties must do the bulk of the work.

collection_notes: No campaign website, so no T2 step. Items from the 2024 OPB District 3 questionnaire (2024-09-30) and the 2022 OPB governor questionnaire (2022-04-14) are older and dated in each statement. Identity match: the 2024 OPB profile (Richmond, age 84, retired mechanical designer, Parks supervisor) matches the 2026 OPB, Mercury (age 86, Parks supervisor) and Tribune (Parks Supervisor, Army National Guard Captain, Multnomah ESD Director) descriptions; the 2022 OPB governor questionnaire lists Portland Parks Supervisor, Oregon Army National Guard Captain and Director, Multnomah ESD, matching the Tribune Q&A. A 2010 Portland Mercury piece about a gun-rights John Sweeney (former parks employee, 28 years Army Guard) was not used because the match is not concrete. Search snippets about 350PDX and bluevoterguide.org were excluded as advocacy material. Homelessness item 1 (OPB 2026) overlaps the existing p3 item, which is tagged social-services.
